title: SC, ST Patients with Annual Family Income of up to ₹5 Lakh Eligible for Medical Assistance under the Revised Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme
subtitle:
Scheme Provides Financial Assistance of up to ₹ 3.50 Lakh to SC and ST Patients for Treatment of Life-Threatening Diseases
Scheme Covers Heart Surgery, Kidney Surgery, Dialysis, Cancer Treatment, Brain Surgery, Organ Transplantation, Spinal Surgery and Other Life-Threatening Diseases
Eligible Beneficiaries To Log In https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/
body_text: The Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is implementing the revised ‘Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme’ , providing financial assistance of up to ₹ 3.50 lakh to eligible patients belonging to the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) suffering from serious and life-threatening diseases. Director DAF Shri Vinesh Pachnanda said the revised scheme, notified on June 2, 2026, aims to improve access to specialised healthcare services and reduce the financial burden of medical treatment on economically vulnerable families. It seeks to ensure that financial constraints do not become a barrier to accessing essential medical treatment and surgical interventions, he said. Shri Pachnanda said under the revised provisions, individuals belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes whose annual family income does not exceed ₹ 5 lakh are eligible to apply for financial assistance. The scheme covers serious ailments related to the kidney, heart, liver, brain and cancer, besides organ transplantation, spinal surgery and other life-threatening diseases requiring medical or surgical intervention, he added. Under the scheme, 100% of the estimated cost of surgery or covered treatment, subject to the prescribed financial ceiling, is released directly to the concerned hospital, Shri Pachnanda added. The Director said the maximum financial assistance admissible is ₹1.50 lakh for heart surgery, ₹3.50 lakh for kidney surgery or dialysis, ₹2.50 lakh for cancer surgery, chemotherapy or radiotherapy, ₹2 lakh for brain surgery, ₹3.50 lakh for kidney or organ transplantation, ₹1.50 lakh for spinal surgery and ₹2 lakh for other life-threatening diseases. The financial assistance may be released in a single instalment before surgery directly to the concerned hospital through RTGS, NEFT or Demand Draft, thereby reducing the immediate financial burden on patients and their families, the Director added. Recognising the financial challenges associated with prolonged medical treatment, the revised scheme also enables patients suffering from chronic ailments to seek a second renewal grant in the subsequent financial year, subject to the applicable provisions, he said. Shri Pachnanda further said a significant provision of the revised scheme is the inclusion of beneficiaries covered under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) who are suffering from renal diseases or require kidney or organ transplantation. Such beneficiaries are also eligible to seek medical assistance under the Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme while other patients covered under PM-JAY are not eligible for assistance under the scheme, he clarified. To facilitate access to specialised medical treatment across the country, the scheme is implemented through a wide network of recognised healthcare institutions, including the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, and AIIMS in other States, all Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)-approved hospitals, hospitals attached to State Government medical colleges, State Government hospitals, hospitals recognised by State Governments and hospitals fully funded by the Central or State Governments, Shri Pachnanda informed. The scheme also covers Government hospitals located at district headquarters and major towns where facilities for the treatment of serious and life-threatening diseases, including organ transplantation and spinal surgery, are available, he added. Shri Pachnanda informed several specialised healthcare institutions, including Sanjay Gandhi Post Graduate Institute, Lucknow; Patna Medical College Hospital, Patna; Jabalpur Hospital and Research Centre, Jabalpur; B. Barua Cancer Institute, Guwahati; Birla Heart Foundation, Kolkata; Kalinga Hospital, Bhubaneswar; Tata Cancer Research Institute, Mumbai; Nizam Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad; and the Voluntary Health Services, Chennai, are also covered under the scheme. In exceptional circumstances, treatment at other hospitals may be considered, subject to the satisfaction of the Chairman of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation regarding the merits of the case, he said. He clarified that applications seeking reimbursement of expenditure already incurred on surgery or medical treatment are ordinarily not entertained. However, reimbursement may be considered on the merits of the case if the application was received by the Foundation at least 15 days before the scheduled date of surgery, he added. Shri Pachnanda said to ensure transparency and accountability in the utilisation of financial assistance, the concerned hospital is required to submit a Utilisation Certificate along with the final medical bills at the time of discharge of the patient. The medical aid released to the hospital must be utilised within one month of its release, and any unutilised or balance amount must be returned to the Foundation at the earliest, but not later than one month after the date of discharge of the patient, he said. The Director DAF informed that eligible beneficiaries may apply for medical assistance through the prescribed application form available on the official website of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF) https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/ or submit an application on plain paper containing the requisite details as specified in the prescribed format. The application must be accompanied by self-attested copies of the latest income certificate, caste certificate and ration card or Aadhaar card of the patient, along with a self-attested passport-size photograph. Applicants are also required to submit the original Estimated Cost Certificate, duly signed by the Medical Superintendent of the concerned hospital, indicating the estimated cost of treatment and the scheduled date of surgery. In cases involving kidney transplantation, applicants are required to furnish additional documents relating to the relationship between the donor and the beneficiary, the prescribed Form 14 pertaining to the decision of the Authorisation Committee and relevant particulars of the kidney donor. The bank account details of the concerned hospital, including the account number, name of the account holder and IFSC code, may also be provided to facilitate the timely processing and direct transfer of financial assistance. The duly completed application, along with the requisite documents, must reach the Director, Dr. Ambedkar Foundation, 15, Janpath, New Delhi – 110001, at least 15 days before the scheduled date of surgery, dialysis or chemotherapy. The Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme serves as an important intervention in addressing the financial barriers faced by economically vulnerable families belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in accessing specialised healthcare services. By extending financial assistance for critical medical interventions, the scheme seeks to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure and facilitate timely access to essential healthcare. Eligible beneficiaries and their family members are encouraged to avail themselves of the benefits under the scheme. Healthcare institutions, State Government departments, social welfare organisations and other stakeholders are also encouraged to disseminate information about the scheme to ensure wider awareness among eligible beneficiaries. For detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria, recognised hospitals and prescribed application forms, interested applicants may visit the official website of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation. https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/ The implementation of the revised Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme reinforces the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to promoting social justice, equitable access to healthcare, financial security and the dignity and well-being of disadvantaged communities, towards the realisation of an inclusive Viksit Bharat@2047 .
